read.sections.0.heading.source: AI can help where helpers are few
read.sections.0.heading.back: AI can help when helpers are not many

read.sections.0.text.source: In many places, there are not enough health workers or other experts for everyone who needs them. AI tools can sometimes help, as in the made-up town of Sunvale, where three tools help with notices, crops and eye checks. Here is a real example from Singapore. People with diabetes need regular eye checks, because the illness can harm their eyes. Researchers there built a tool called SELENA+, which looks at photos of the back of the eye and marks the ones an eye specialist should see. In 2017, they reported tests with photos from Singapore's eye checks and from people in other countries. It found most of the problems that trained checkers found, but the researchers said it still needed testing in real clinics.
read.sections.0.text.back: In many places, there are not enough health workers or other experts for everyone who needs them. AI tools can sometimes help, as in the made-up town of Sunvale, where three tools help with notices, crops and eye checks. Here is a real example from Singapore. People who have diabetes ("kencing manis") need to check their eyes regularly, because the illness can damage their eyes. Researchers there built a tool called SELENA+, which looks at photos of the back of the eye and marks the photos an eye specialist should see. In 2017, they reported tests with photos from eye checks in Singapore and from people in other countries. The tool found most of the problems found by trained checkers, but the researchers said it still needed to be tested in real clinics.
read.sections.0.text.note: "Diabetes" is followed by the everyday Malaysian name "kencing manis" in brackets, in both texts, so young readers know it; a reviewer may prefer one or the other.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: Many places do not have enough health workers or other experts. AI tools can sometimes help. In made-up Sunvale, three tools help with notices, plants and eyes. In Singapore, researchers built a real tool called SELENA+. People with diabetes need eye checks, because the illness can harm their eyes. SELENA+ marks eye photos that an eye doctor should see. In 2017, it was tested on photos from Singapore and elsewhere. It found most problems that people found. It still needed tests in real clinics.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: Many places do not have enough health workers or other experts. AI tools can sometimes help. In Sunvale, a made-up town, three tools help with notices, plants and eyes. In Singapore, researchers built a real tool called SELENA+. People who have diabetes ("kencing manis") need to check their eyes. The illness can damage their eyes. SELENA+ marks eye photos that an eye doctor should see. In 2017, it was tested with photos from Singapore and other places. It found most problems that humans found. It still needs to be tested in real clinics.
read.sections.0.simpler.note: The English has "people found"; "manusia" (humans) keeps the contrast with the tool.

read.sections.1.text.source: A tool that helps can also cause problems, so it is important to weigh the benefits against the risks. The Sunvale eye helper learned mostly from photos of people in other places. That does not make it a poor tool. But nobody has tested it in Sunvale, so it might miss some problems there. A tool must be tested with the people it will serve. Translation tools make more mistakes in languages with little writing online. A farmer who trusts a wrong guess might pull out healthy plants. Health photos are also private, so they must be kept safe.
read.sections.1.text.back: A tool that helps can also cause problems, so we need to weigh the benefits against its risks. The Sunvale eye helper mostly learned from photos of people in other places. That does not make it a weak tool. But nobody has tested it in Sunvale, so it might miss some problems there. A tool must be tested with the people who will use it. Translation tools make more mistakes in languages that have little writing online. A farmer who believes a wrong guess might pull out healthy plants. Health photos are also private information, so they must be kept safely.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: A tool that helps can also cause problems. So weigh the benefits and the risks. The eye helper learned from people in other places. That does not make it bad. But nobody has tested it in Sunvale. It might miss problems there. Tools must be tested with the people they help. Translation tools make more mistakes in some languages. A farmer could trust a wrong guess. Health photos are private and must be kept safe.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: A tool that helps can also cause problems. So weigh the benefits and its risks. The eye helper learned from people in other places. That does not make it bad. But nobody has tested it in Sunvale. It might miss problems there. Tools must be tested with the people they help. Translation tools make more mistakes in some languages. A farmer might believe a wrong guess. Health photos are private information and must be kept safely.

read.sections.2.heading.note: "Stay in charge" is "terus memegang kawalan" (keep holding control); a reviewer may prefer "kekal berkuasa membuat keputusan".

read.sections.2.text.source: Because AI tools can be wrong, people need to stay in charge of important decisions. In Sunvale, a volunteer who speaks the language checks important translated notices. A plant expert helps when the leaf tool isn't sure, and a health worker always checks the eye helper. The people of a community should also help to shape the tools they use. Before trusting any AI tool, ask three questions. Who does it help? Who might it leave out? Who checks its answers? For any health question, always ask a health worker, not a tool.
read.sections.2.text.back: Because AI tools can be wrong, people need to keep holding control over important decisions. In Sunvale, a volunteer who speaks the language checks important notices that have been translated. A plant expert helps when the leaf tool is not sure, and a health worker always checks the eye helper. The people of a community should also help to shape the tools they use. Before trusting any AI tool, ask three questions. Whom does it help? Who might be left behind? Who checks its answers? For any question about health, always ask a health worker, not a tool.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: AI tools can be wrong. So people must stay in charge of big decisions. In Sunvale, a volunteer checks notices. An expert and a health worker check the other tools. People in a community should help shape their tools. Ask three questions. Who does it help? Who might it leave out? Who checks it? For health questions, ask a health worker.

An expert and a health worker check the other tools. People in a community should help shape their tools. Ask three questions. Whom does it help? Who might be left behind? Who checks it? For health questions, ask a health worker.

watch.summary.source: In this video, people who build and study AI talk about fairness. AI tools learn from data, and they are already used in many parts of life. The speakers say AI could help more people get what they need. But AI can also be unfair. If the data, or the people who build a tool, leave some groups out, the tool can work worse for those groups or treat them unfairly. This is called algorithmic bias. The speakers say that people from many different backgrounds should help to build AI. They also say that people must keep checking AI tools, so that the tools help everyone and don't harm the people they leave out.

The speakers say AI can help more people get what they need. But AI can also be unfair. The speakers say people from many different backgrounds should help build AI. They also say people must keep checking AI tools, so that the tools help everyone and do not harm the people they leave out.

educatorNotes.0.source: The Sunvale tools are made up and stay labelled; SELENA+ is real and appears only in the reading, never in the made-up evidence or activity. What the sources establish: SNEC's page says SELENA+ was developed with about 500,000 retina photos and checked on 10 outside sets of photos (different cameras, ethnic groups and ages), and is approved by Singapore's health products regulator and CE-marked. The 2017 JAMA study tested it on 14,880 patients' photos from Singapore's national diabetic eye screening programme and on 10 other groups; it found referable eye disease with high sensitivity and specificity compared with trained graders, and said more research was needed for use in health care. The developers' own 2024 case study (Gunasekeran and others, NEJM AI) describes putting it into that programme; the lesson does not claim rollout or patient results, because no independent evaluation was checked. Other real projects, for teachers only: an offline cassava-disease phone app by IITA and Penn State (2018); WHO's 2021 report on AI for health; CLEAR Global's human checking of language technology.
educatorNotes.0.back: The Sunvale tools are made up and stay labelled; SELENA+ is real and appears only in the reading, never in the made-up evidence or activity. What the sources establish: SNEC's page states that SELENA+ was developed with about 500,000 retina photos and checked with 10 sets of photos from outside (different cameras, ethnic groups and ages), and is approved by Singapore's health products regulator and has a CE mark. The 2017 JAMA study tested it with photos of 14,880 patients from Singapore's national diabetic eye screening programme and with 10 other groups; it detected eye disease that should be referred with high sensitivity and specificity compared with trained checkers, and stated that more research is needed for use in health care. The developers' own 2024 case study (Gunasekeran and colleagues, NEJM AI) explains how it was put into that programme; this lesson makes no claim about rollout or patient results, because no independent evaluation was checked. Other real projects, for teachers only: an offline phone app for cassava disease by IITA and Penn State (2018); WHO's 2021 report on AI for health; human checking by CLEAR Global of language technology.
